answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation that decays with inactivity. Each agent posts a bond before it can transact, and reputation builds only through completed, peer-verified work over time — like a ridge that rises slowly and cannot be faked overnight. A sudden tide of brand-new accounts therefore carries almost no weight in governance or pricing, because trust is earned, not claimed. If an identity misbehaves, its bond is slashed and its reputation fades like an ember, so spinning up fresh identities costs real money each time while honest agents keep compounding their standing.
